architecture_decisions: Deterministic two-commit baseline, zero persistent bootstrap source, exact repository scope, REVIEW-only mutation authority
work_items: Contents API remains the one empty-repository bootstrap primitive
validations: Preserve the accepted deterministic two-commit baseline, zero persistent bootstrap source, exact repository scope, REVIEW-only mutation authority

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The authoritative state records exact `.36` merge/deployment/health/readiness evidence, that `TARGET_DISCOVERY_UNBOUNDED` did not recur, and that the later greenfield `PROVIDER_CONFLICT` arose after successful marker creation and Vercel Project readiness. It does not claim W9-S1 completion.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — A permanent regression models the observed provider behavior: deleting the sole Contents path may return HTTP 200 while subsequent Git ref/commit reads return empty-repository 409. The corrected initializer no longer depends on Contents DELETE to produce the durable cleanup commit.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Tests prove truly empty state performs exactly one fixed Contents `PUT` before any Git Database mutation and validates returned root commit/blob plus exact default-ref/root-tree read-back.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Tests prove Git tree creation uses the verified bootstrap tree as `base_tree` and one exact `.parallax-greenfield` entry with `sha: null`; returned/read-back cleanup tree is empty. Extra/malformed/truncated tree state fails closed.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Tests prove the cleanup commit uses the fixed cleanup message/actor, verified empty tree and exactly one parent equal to the bootstrap root. Wrong parent/tree/message/actor or malformed returned identity fails before ref mutation.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Tests prove the canonical default ref must equal bootstrap immediately before update and is patched only to the verified cleanup commit with `force=false`. Ref drift, 409/422 without exact idempotent read-back, wrong final head or any attempted force update fails closed.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Tests prove an already-existing exact two-commit baseline is accepted using GET-only verification and no mutation. Unrelated, partial, mismatched or arbitrary empty history is rejected.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Focused/full regressions prove positive empty inspection, zero-file root lineage, non-empty implementation, accepted lineage, exact Git branch/commit/PR delivery, Vercel Preview exactness, commit-bearing source paths and source-only delivery remain unchanged outside the corrected initializer.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Diff and release review prove no provider/connector/repository coverage addition, no GitHub permission beyond existing delivery authority, no arbitrary Git mutation surface, no force ref update, no direct default-branch accepted-source publication, and no REVIEW/merge/production authority expansion.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Protected PR and post-merge gates pass on exact heads; corrected API source reaches production READY; canonical `/health` and `/ready` return HTTP 200; production preflights pass; exact-deployment warning/error/fatal verification reveals no unresolved release blocker.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — The same frozen W9-S1 Project/Work Specification/Engineering Run is retried where canonical state permits. Exact production evidence proves the baseline no longer fails at the old Contents-delete/ref/cleanup-commit `PROVIDER_CONFLICT`. Successful branch/commit/PR/Preview publication may satisfy the benchmark only up to the unchanged human REVIEW boundary. Any genuinely later independent blocker is recorded separately.
